# Nltest Domain Trust or Domain Controller Discovery

`win_proc_nltest_domain_trust_discovery` · Sigma id `1396e2ee-416e-448c-a2ac-e7f13ad55915` · status `experimental` · level `medium`

## Goal

Catch an intruder mapping Active Directory soon after getting a foothold: listing domain trusts and domain controllers to decide where to go next. It's an early warning, often hours before the damaging steps.

## ATT&CK

- [T1482](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1482/) Domain Trust Discovery
- Tactic: Discovery (TA0007)

Checked against pinned ATT&CK v20.1 by `ringtail validate`.

## Log source

product: `windows`, category: `process_creation`

## Detection logic

Fires when nltest (matched by path or original file name) runs with /domain_trusts, /all_trusts, /trusted_domains, or /dclist. Dash or slash style both count. Routine helpdesk uses such as checking the secure channel (/sc_query) or locating a DC (/dsgetdc) don't fire.

Exact logic, generated from the rule:

- **selection_img**: any one of
  - `Image` ends with `'\nltest.exe'`
  - `OriginalFileName` is `'nltestrk.exe'`
- **selection_cli**: `CommandLine` contains any of `'-domain_trusts'`, `'-all_trusts'`, `'-trusted_domains'`, `'-dclist'` (also matches `/` and Unicode dash look-alikes in place of `-`)
- **Condition**: `all of selection_*`

**Splunk (SPL)**: Windows event and Sysmon field names (Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows / Sysmon)

```spl
(Image="*\\nltest.exe" OR OriginalFileName="nltestrk.exe") (CommandLine="*-domain_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*/domain_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*–domain_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*—domain_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*―domain_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*-all_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*/all_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*–all_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*—all_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*―all_trusts*" OR CommandLine="*-trusted_domains*" OR CommandLine="*/trusted_domains*" OR CommandLine="*–trusted_domains*" OR CommandLine="*—trusted_domains*" OR CommandLine="*―trusted_domains*" OR CommandLine="*-dclist*" OR CommandLine="*/dclist*" OR CommandLine="*–dclist*" OR CommandLine="*—dclist*" OR CommandLine="*―dclist*")
```

**Microsoft Sentinel / Defender XDR (KQL)**: Defender XDR DeviceProcessEvents (also in Sentinel with the Defender XDR connector)

```kql
DeviceProcessEvents
| where (FolderPath endswith "\\nltest.exe" or ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName =~ "nltestrk.exe") and (ProcessCommandLine contains "-domain_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/domain_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–domain_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—domain_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―domain_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-all_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/all_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–all_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—all_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―all_trusts" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-trusted_domains" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/trusted_domains" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–trusted_domains" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—trusted_domains" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―trusted_domains" or ProcessCommandLine contains "-dclist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "/dclist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "–dclist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "—dclist" or ProcessCommandLine contains "―dclist")
```

## Known false positives

- Domain administrators and AD health scripts checking trusts (expect a short, known list of admin accounts and hosts)

## Triage steps

1. Check who ran it and from where. Domain admins on admin workstations or a known AD health script are plausible. A regular user's workstation, or nltest spawned by an unusual parent (an unknown executable in AppData or Temp, Office, a script host), is not.
2. Look for other discovery on the same host within the hour: systeminfo, whoami /groups, net group "domain admins", AdFind, or BloodHound collectors. Several together is a strong signal of an intruder.
3. Trace the parent process back to how it started: a loader, a phishing attachment, or a remote access tool. That's your initial access.
4. Coverage gap: this rule only covers nltest. PowerShell (Get-ADTrust), AdFind, and BloodHound do the same discovery and need their own rules.

## Test results

**PASS**: 3/3 true-positive samples matched, 3/3 false-positive samples correctly ignored.

| Sample | Should fire | Fired | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trust enumeration from a beachhead, spawned by an injected process. | yes | yes | pass |
| Domain controller list. | yes | yes | pass |
| Renamed copy, dash-style switch. | yes | yes | pass |
| Near miss: nltest checking the secure channel, a routine helpdesk fix. | no | no | pass |
| Near miss: nltest locating a DC for the user's own domain. | no | no | pass |
| Out of scope: the PowerShell AD module listing trusts. A different tool; this rule is nltest-only (see the card). | no | no | pass |
